mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an easing monetary policy cycle, which lowers discount rates on equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 4% signals tight labor markets, raising inflation expectations and compressing equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite UNRATE rising above 4%, or the effect fades within the 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) proxies indicates robust demand growth, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and HOUST increase over the next month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both GDPC1 and HOUST increasing, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle regime, a sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 3% triggers higher discount rates on equities, compressing future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS rising above 3%, or the effect reverses in the tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in the supply index (INDPRO) below 100 signals reduced production capacity, leading to higher inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite INDPRO dropping below 100, or the contraction effect is short-lived.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment (UNRATE) rates above 4% creates conflicting labor market signals, but their combined effect in a tightening cycle reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase above 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite both PAYEMS and UNRATE rising above 4%, or the conflicting signals negate the expected impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the supply index (INDPRO) above 100 reflects expanding production capacity, boosting future growth prospects and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite INDPRO rising, or the supply expansion does not materialize as expected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained drop in housing demand (HOUST) below 1600 units signals overexpansion, leading to reduced growth expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) despite HOUST dropping below 1600 in a late-cycle expansion, or the signal is not sustained.
